_comment: Every ground the era models were trained on -- all 17, up from a hand-picked 10. The six that were missing (Pune, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, DY Patil, Sharjah, Brabourne) plus Mullanpur had real measured profiles the game simply never offered; Dubai alone has more 2014-2022 balls than Eden Gardens. Ids match ml/runtime/venues.py's canonical map, which is also what ml/etl/venue_types.py keys its profiles on, so a ground added here resolves to real per-era data instead of the league fallback.
_pitch_labels: DERIVED FROM MEASUREMENT, not hand-authored. Aggregated over all three eras: |spin-pace edge| >= 0.30 makes a ground dusty or green, otherwise boundary share against the 59.7% league mean makes it flat or slow. Several old labels were simply wrong -- Rajiv Gandhi (Uppal) was typed `slow` and is the most PACE-friendly ground in the league at +0.53, and Arun Jaitley was typed `slow` but spin bites there at -0.33.
_what_the_label_does: It drives the card text and the classic engine's PITCH_EFFECTS only. The learned model never reads it -- it takes the MEASURED numbers (runs/ball, wickets/ball, boundary share, and the residualised spin/pace edge for the bowler's own type) straight from ml/artifacts/eras/<era>/venue_profile.json. So a label being a judgement call cannot corrupt the simulation.

pitch_types.dusty: Dust bowl — turns square, spinners are lethal
pitch_types.green: Green seamer — nip, bounce and movement for pacers
pitch_types.flat: Flat road — batting paradise, boundaries flow
pitch_types.slow: Slow and low — timing is hard, run-making is a grind
